data.title: 646 Crypto Cards Reviewed: Issuers and Costs Matter More Than Headline Cashback
data.description: An assessment of 646 crypto cards found that only 256 were suitable for general users, while 91 were classified as high risk, including 57 with no KYC requirement. According to PANews, just four of the 109 cards that received scores earned an S rating, with ether.fi Cash ranking first at 78.5 points. High cashback offers often come with conditions such as token payouts, lockups, or high asset thresholds; the assessment identified issuers and actual costs as key evaluation criteria.

data.title: Maple CEO Says Co-Founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan Are Leaving, Operations Continue Normally
data.description: Maple Finance CEO and co-founder Sid Powell said co-founder Joe Flanagan and Chief Operating Officer Ryan have decided to leave the company. According to PANews, which reported the news on November 14, the departures follow differences over the company’s future direction, and Flanagan will support the transition through the end of 2026. Powell said he respects their decision, will continue leading the team, and that Maple’s operations will continue normally. He said the company will focus on on-chain credit and the integration of decentralized finance with traditional finance and fintech, with plans to increase investment over the next year in on-chain credit, yield products, embedded services, vaults, and tokenized collateral.

data.title: CFTC Sues Louisiana to Challenge Prediction Market Ban
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing an announcement by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the agency has sued Louisiana to block the state from barring CFTC-regulated exchanges and other entities from offering event contracts.

The CFTC said a Louisiana court had ordered more than 30 companies involved in CFTC-regulated derivatives trading to stop operating in the state without notifying the defendants or giving them an opportunity to be heard. Louisiana is the 12th state the agency has sued as it seeks to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over derivatives markets.

data.title: Securitize Files SEC Comment Letter Supporting Exemption for Tokenized Securities AMM Trading
data.description: Securitize co-founder and CEO Carlos Domingo said the company filed a comment letter with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission supporting a conditional exemption for tokenized securities trading venues. According to Odaily, the proposed exemption would last five years and allow eligible venues to trade some tokenized U.S. stocks through access-restricted automated market makers (AMMs) and liquidity pools. Securitize supports giving tokenized shares the same dividends, voting rights and economic rights as their corresponding shares, and recommends embedding compliance rules in the tokens so restrictions remain in effect after transfers.

data.title: Solana and TryNitoAI Partner to Develop Privacy-Focused AI Tool With Verifiable On-Chain Hardware Attestation
data.description: Solana Confidential Compute is an open-source tool for privacy-focused AI development that supports verifiable on-chain hardware attestation. According to Odaily, Solana and TryNitoAI developed the tool, which developers can use to build personal assistants, agents that handle sensitive business data, and private trading strategies.

data.title: Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson Says Inflation Will Guide Rate Decisions
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said inflation has become the most important measure for policymakers weighing whether to raise interest rates further. He noted that economic activity and the labor market have remained strong recently, while price pressures persist. Jefferson said the inflation outlook will provide an important signal for monetary policy, and policymakers should follow economic data when deciding whether to adjust policy. Several Fed officials expressed concern about price pressures this week, while markets expect a rate hike in December.

data.title: Paraguay to End Special Power Contracts Covering 943.8 MW Used by Crypto Miners
data.description: Paraguay’s National Electricity Administration (ANDE) said special power contracts for high-energy users, including cryptocurrency miners, will end on December 31, 2027, and will not be renewed under current regulations. According to Odaily, the operators collectively use 943.8 megawatts of Paraguay’s surplus hydropower, and the change is expected to significantly affect HIVE Digital Technologies, which has about 77% to 80% of its active mining capacity in the country. ANDE is also signing 15-year power supply agreements with AI data centers.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Anthropic IPO Faces Scrutiny After Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down
data.description:
Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO faces added scrutiny after Nvidia co-founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday, following reports that he was involved in two extramarital affairs. The IPO is seen as a test of investor appetite for the AI sector.

According to Sina Finance, Anthropic is expected to list next Wednesday or Thursday, days after Nvidia reports earnings for the first time without Huang at the helm. Nvidia is a close Anthropic partner and has agreed to buy about $10 billion in shares through a $26 billion private placement concurrent with the IPO, according to Anthropic’s filing. Anthropic has committed billions of dollars for access to Nvidia’s advanced chips.

Investors and analysts said the Nvidia turmoil is unlikely to affect Anthropic’s core business but could influence the broader narrative around AI. Jay Goldberg, an analyst at Seaport Research Partners and one of the few Wall Street analysts with a sell rating on Nvidia, said Huang’s departure would not stop the IPO. He said greater risk could emerge after listing, when Anthropic releases its first quarterly results and investors may question whether the AI rally can continue.

M13 partner Carl Almar said Anthropic’s fundamentals remained solid, citing strong company data, ample computing capacity and controlled spending. Anthropic is less dependent on Nvidia than many peers: some of its models also run on Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium chips and AMD GPUs. The company is also reportedly developing its own chips.

Francine McKenna, an accountant and investigative journalist who teaches at the Wharton School, said Nvidia’s $10 billion commitment was likely to proceed, but investors who expected Nvidia to support CoreWeave might need another backer. Georgetown professor Jason Schletzer said scrutiny of Anthropic’s ties to Nvidia and Nvidia-linked customers could increase.

With more than 400 investors involved, the IPO is a high-stakes liquidity event for Silicon Valley’s AI-focused private market. Market participants broadly view a successful listing as positive for the AI rally, while a weak reception or indefinite delay could signal that the boom is nearing a bubble break. One anonymous venture investor said Anthropic could benefit because its CEO, Dario Amodei, has differed with Huang on AI regulation, and the company’s chip development could open up supply-chain capacity.

data.title: Nina Trentmann: Colette Kress Faces Scrutiny as Nvidia Interim CEO
data.description: Nina Trentmann, a senior editor at Bloomberg News, said Colette Kress is likely to become more visible as Nvidia’s interim CEO after Jensen Huang’s departure, speaking more about the company’s finances, performance and plans, according to Bloomberg. Trentmann spoke with Vonnie Quinn on “The Close.”

data.title: SpaceX Starship Lifts Off for Flight Test of Reusability
data.description: SpaceX’s Starship lifted off from the Starbase launch facility in South Texas for a flight test aimed at bringing both sections of the vehicle safely back to Earth, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Musk Says He Will Sign Petition to Reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Elon Musk said on X that a petition calling for Jensen Huang to return as Nvidia CEO is underway and that he would sign it. The post Musk replied to was published by X user Yun-Ta Tsai, who argued that Nvidia employees should resign en masse if they want Huang back, saying GPU engineers are harder to find and replace than machine-learning engineers and that engineers, not the board, determine the company’s mission. Nvidia employees had previously launched a petition calling for Huang to return as CEO.

data.title: AI | Morgan Stanley’s Lisa Shalett Stays Bullish on AI Spending Despite Turmoil
data.description: Nvidia Corp.’s leadership turmoil and Democrats’ midterm election victories have added to concerns about the artificial intelligence boom, but Morgan Stanley Wealth Management’s Lisa Shalett said they won’t derail capital spending on AI infrastructure, the main driver of the bull market, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Exemplar Luxury Group CEO Says Company Is Stronger After Saks Emerged From Bankruptcy
data.description: Geoffroy van Raemdonck said Exemplar Luxury Group is financially stronger after Saks emerged from bankruptcy, Bloomberg reported. He said customer loyalty, full-price sales and profitable growth helped achieve that goal, supporting reinvestment and stronger relationships with brands.

data.title: Climate Change Outpaces Scientists’ Predictions as COP31 Seeks Emissions Goals
data.description: COP31 aims to set new goals to reduce emissions as climate change outpaces scientists’ predictions and disasters drive billions of dollars in losses, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Jeff Currie Says China Is Behind His Bearish Copper View
data.description:
Jeff Currie said he is bearish on copper because of China, according to Bloomberg. Currie is CEO and founder of Real Macro and a senior adviser at Carlyle.

In an interview with Vonnie Quinn and Bailey Lipschultz on “The Close,” he said gold’s retreat reflects a shortage of dollar liquidity and discussed the global oil industry.

data.title: Polkadot Community Approves New Strategy With 97% Vote, Prioritizing Product Platform and DotUSD
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Polkadot’s decentralized governance system approved a new strategy proposed by the Polkadot Community Foundation (PCF) on November 11, with 97% of votes in favor. The strategy prioritizes the upcoming Polkadot product platform and direct user acquisition, under a mandate confirmed by DOTDAO.

The platform is intended to prioritize user privacy and data rights. PCF plans to launch its first mobile-focused offering through the Polkadot App, supporting private messaging and digital cash payments. The strategy starts its DOT-backed dotStables with dotUSD, designed to track the U.S. dollar and build value for DOT through usage. The Polkadot Technical Fellowship will oversee dotUSD and other dotStables, alongside independent audits and risk management.

The strategy also shifts shared funding and resources away from general marketing toward incentives tied to measurable user engagement. Its stated aim is for product use to drive demand for DOT-backed dotStables, ultimately translating into demand for DOT.

data.title: AI | Match Group CEO Spencer Rascoff Says AI Agents Won’t Date for Users
data.description: Match Group CEO Spencer Rascoff says AI agents will not be allowed to date on behalf of users on Tinder, Hinge and the company’s other apps, which he calls a “human-only zone,” according to Bloomberg. Match uses AI to verify identities, improve safety and block harmful messages. Rascoff discussed where companies should draw the line on AI, how the technology is changing Match Group, Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia and why he believes companies are bigger than any one CEO.

data.title: AI | Blackstone-Backed QTS Cuts Planned AI Debt Sale by About 60%
data.description: QTS, a data center operator backed by Blackstone Inc., is reducing the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60% after struggling to attract enough investor demand and refusing to pay much higher yields, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: FAA Halts U.S. Departures Nationwide, Raising Risk for Airline Stocks
data.description: The FAA ordered a nationwide halt to U.S. flight departures after an air traffic control communications failure, raising concerns about airline stocks. The order came around 3:54 p.m. Eastern on Friday, November 13, six minutes before Wall Street closed, according to BeInCrypto. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said communications problems were affecting regional air traffic control centers; the FAA had halted traffic in Chicago shortly before the nationwide order. Aircraft already airborne could continue to land, while international arrivals would be handled individually. Technicians were investigating, with no cause or restart time announced. A Microsoft 365 outage affecting Outlook and Teams since Thursday continued Friday, but no connection to the FAA failure was confirmed. Before the grounding, United Airlines fell 6.0%, American Airlines dropped 5.6% and Delta Air Lines lost 5.2% on Thursday. The Nasdaq fell 0.9% and the S&P 500 declined 0.4% on Friday. The late FAA announcement left little time for a meaningful regular-session market reaction. Extended cancellations could increase airline costs and disrupt schedules, with Monday’s market reopening potentially providing an initial test if the communications problems persist through the weekend.

data.title: US Struggles to Build Affordable Housing as Construction Costs Rise
data.description: Boston Fed Principal Economist and Policy Advisor Paul Willen says soaring construction costs are making many approved housing projects financially unworkable, according to Bloomberg. He points to research showing construction productivity has barely improved in decades, while productivity across much of the rest of the economy has surged.
